title: What makes a musician great, and reading with Troy Floyd
summary: Willis Santiago and Caffery Darensbourg as all-round greats; Albert mostly read parts in Troy Floyd's band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Let me move all this stuff and get it out of your way.
Willis, Santiago, I'm doubt seriously, was what we would call a great musician before. He was an artist. Yeah. He was a great artist.
Well, what made somebody like him great?
Well, I guess you'd call it natural ability. A guy's just born with a natural gift.
Could he play fast or did he? Play anything.

He's played old Tom Anderson's cafe up here where Cress is up on. Yeah. And that was days when Bonnie was with a real young fella, Paul Byrd, and they had a tremendous little band there. And that's where Bonnie and Alvin Nicholas left and went up to Chicago to join. King Oliver.

Well, it strikes me, you know, when I talk to New Orleans musicians, I never know exactly when they say somebody's great, exactly what the man was great at. Some guys are great at, say, you take Caffrey Dyer and Jerry. I don't know if he was great at keeping a beat with the correct chord changes.

No, he was great in everything. He could solo, he could chord, and he could improvise his own ideas. Which, all in all, that's what you say when you say a man is great. Yeah, all in all. All in all. Now you might have some musician that's great in soloing only. Yeah. But as far as being able to tie himself in with the other musicians, no. Yeah. Well, that fella, you can't consider him as great. Mm-hmm. Because he's confined to one thing only. Yeah.
Well, some people are great readers but can't play, you know. That's true.

Yeah. A lot of, well, for instance, for a long time, when I was with Troy First, joined Troy Floyd's band, I didn't have too much time for solo work. Yeah. Most of mine was reading because the fellas in the band were limited. And of course, naturally, I had to play three, four, five different parts. Yeah. But as the band got older and we got to playing together, well then I could occasionally get out and solo.
Mm-hmm. Well, you must have been an awful good soloist, changing from the rapids. There's so many things.

Well, the training that I had is responsible for it. Well, for instance, my daddy was a musician and in fact, most of my family were musicians. But staying right there with Manuel Perez, Milford Piron, old man Gus Moret, and people like that, and you have to learn, otherwise you don't have nothing in your head if you can't learn with these fellas. George Moret. Old man George Moret. Yeah.
